sample_question.question_text: In Breadth-First Search, if the branching factor is b and depth of shallowest solution is d, what is the space complexity?
sample_question.explanation: BFS stores all generated nodes in memory at the current frontier level. At depth d, there are b^d leaf nodes in memory. Hence space complexity is O(b^d).
sample_question.numerical_formula: Time Complexity of BFS = O(b^d), Space = O(b^d)
sample_question.real_time_application: GPS Navigation routing in sparse road networks; Web crawler link traversal.

sample_question.question_text: In the ID3 algorithm, if a dataset S has 9 positive and 5 negative examples, the entropy Entropy(S) is calculated using:
sample_question.explanation: Shannon Entropy is defined as -Sum(p_i * log2(p_i)). With p(+) = 9/14 and p(-) = 5/14, Entropy = -(9/14)*log2(9/14) - (5/14)*log2(5/14) approx 0.940 bits.
sample_question.numerical_formula: Gain(S, A) = Entropy(S) - Sum_{v} (|S_v| / |S|) * Entropy(S_v)

nodes.key_formula: Principal components are eigenvectors of covariance matrix Sigma = (1/N) * X^T * X
nodes.real_time_application: Facial recognition feature compression (Eigenfaces) and financial risk factor analysis.

sample_question.question_text: In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the first principal component corresponds to:
sample_question.option_a: The eigenvector associated with the smallest eigenvalue
sample_question.option_b: The eigenvector associated with the largest eigenvalue
sample_question.option_c: The mean of the feature vector
sample_question.option_d: The determinant of the covariance matrix

sample_question.question_text: In the Transformer attention mechanism, why is the dot product Q * K^T scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k)?
sample_question.option_a: To convert vectors to unit length
sample_question.option_b: To prevent extremely large values that push the Softmax function into regions with near-zero gradients
sample_question.option_c: To eliminate the need for positional encoding
sample_question.explanation: For large key dimensions d_k, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) stabilizes the gradient flow.
sample_question.numerical_formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V
